clue.text: Standard pain not entirely ideal

parts.note: par is the standard score, as in golf

indicators.note: not entirely tells us to drop the final letter of the word for pain

parts.note: agony is great pain

explanation.surface: A grumble that the usual level of discomfort is far from ideal.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is a model of perfection, so used as a noun it is an ideal.

clue.text: Riddle, corny stuff?

definitions.meaning: to riddle is to fill full of holes, as with bullets
a spice that comes as corns, ground from peppercorns

explanation.surface: A riddle that is rather corny.
explanation.definitionFit: To pepper is to riddle with shot, and the spice is made from corns, the dried berries.

clue.text: Method majestic sovereign set up

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means read from bottom to top, so the pieces are turned round

parts.note: epic means grand or majestic
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for a queen as sovereign

explanation.surface: A procedure established by a grand monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses EPICER, the pieces in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipe is a set of instructions, hence a method for producing something.

clue.text: Actor, part of one's make-up less restrained

parts.note: a gene is part of one's genetic make-up
wilder means less restrained

explanation.surface: A performer whose nature has grown less inhibited.
explanation.definitionFit: Gene Wilder was an American comic film performer, star of Willy Wonka.

clue.text: King released from pound, more agreeable

indicators.note: released from means the king's letter is let out of the word for pound

parts.note: nicker is British slang for a pound sterling
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch freed from an enclosure is in better humour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' suggests an animal enclosure, but it is money: nicker is British slang for a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicer is the comparative of nice, meaning pleasanter.

clue.text: Hugging skill backfiring, kiss — this kept up one's sleeve?

indicators.note: one word hugging another holds it inside, so the kiss surrounds the skill

parts.note: snog is British slang for a long kiss

indicators.note: backfiring means the word for skill is read backwards

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: A cuddle and kiss that go wrong, with something tucked up a sleeve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backfiring' turns ART into TRA, and SNOG hugs it. A snot-rag is crude slang for a handkerchief, traditionally kept up the sleeve.
explanation.definitionFit: A handkerchief is famously tucked up a sleeve, and snot rag is a vulgar name for one.

clue.text: Plain figure in the end dividing complex integers

indicators.note: dividing means that final letter splits the jumbled letters
complex means the letters of integers are tangled into a new order
in the end means take the final letter of the word figure

explanation.surface: A maths lesson: a plain figure ending up dividing complex numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' rearranges INTEGERS and the E from 'figure in the end' goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti is a vast grassland plain in Tanzania and Kenya.

clue.text: Load of extra money skimmed

indicators.note: skimmed means the top letter is taken off, as cream is skimmed from milk

parts.note: a bonus is extra money

explanation.surface: A sum of extra cash with some taken off the top.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a burden or responsibility, figuratively a load.

clue.text: People eating European cheese dish

indicators.note: eating means the people take the European inside them

parts.note: a race is a people
a Lett is a Latvian, a European

explanation.surface: Diners sharing a European cheese dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Raclette is a Swiss dish of melted cheese scraped onto potatoes.

clue.text: Author Ray after centre parting, leaves

parts.note: Graham Greene was an English novelist

indicators.note: after its centre parts means the middle letter of ray is removed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A novelist named Ray with his hair parted in the middle leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb but is foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenery is green foliage, and leaves are foliage.

clue.text: What is able to keep children fit? A nut!

parts.note: PE, physical education, is the school subject that keeps children fit
can means is able

explanation.surface: A cheery suggestion that a nut is the snack to keep children healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: The pecan is a nut from a hickory tree native to North America.

clue.text: Painful thing seeing a couple almost knocked over by relative

indicators.note: by places the relative next to the reversed letters
knocked over means the shortened word is turned the other way round
almost means the last letter of the word for a couple is dropped

parts.note: a brace is a pair, as of game birds
an uncle is a relative

explanation.surface: A pair of people bowled over by a family member, which hurts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts BRACE to BRAC and 'knocked over' turns that to CARB.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbuncle is a painful boil or abscess on the skin.

clue.text: Permit banning it, we go in clumsily — that's providing authorisation

indicators.note: clumsily means the letters are put together awkwardly in a new order
banning means the word it is barred from the word permit

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone barging in despite a permit forbidding it, while claiming authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banning' takes IT out of PERMIT, leaving PERM; 'clumsily' rearranges PERM and WEGOIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To empower someone is to give them authority, so the participle means granting authorisation.

clue.text: In chlorine, one finds a gas

indicators.note: in says the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A chemistry fact: within chlorine one finds a gas.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites thinking about chemistry; the letters sit across 'chlorine, one'.
explanation.definitionFit: Neon is a noble gas, element number ten, used in glowing signs.

clue.text: Control said to be brought back

parts.note: rein means control, as in rein in
stated means said

explanation.surface: Restraint, it is said, is to be restored.
explanation.definitionFit: Reinstated means restored to a former position, so brought back.

clue.text: Might one recognise a story that is by man who talks backwards embraced by reader?

indicators.note: embraced by means the following pieces are held inside the word for reader

parts.note: a lector is a reader, especially of lessons in church
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

indicators.note: backwards means the man's name is read the other way round

parts.note: Ted, a man's name, also gives TED Talks, the lecture series

explanation.surface: A puzzling picture of a reader hugging a storyteller who speaks backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man who talks' points at TED Talks; 'backwards' turns his name round. The 'story' in the definition is a fib, which a polygraph aims to catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A polygraph is meant to spot falsehoods, and a story is a fib, so it might recognise one.

clue.text: Fancy getting flesh out

definitions.meaning: fancy as an adjective means intricate or ornate
to flesh out is to add detail to

explanation.surface: Imagine getting meat out of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaborate as an adjective is ornate, and as a verb it means to develop with more detail.

clue.text: Green initiative's ultimate supporter getting item in a column

parts.note: vert is green in heraldry

indicators.note: ultimate means take the last letter of the word initiative

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: An environmental scheme's ultimate backer finds a place in a newspaper column.
explanation.walkthrough: 'column' is the spinal column, not a newspaper's.
explanation.definitionFit: A vertebra is one of the bones that make up the spinal column.

clue.text: 1 Aug and solver finally cracking this puzzle here

indicators.note: cracking means the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: the numeral one looks like the letter I
taken as written

indicators.note: finally means take the last letter of solver

explanation.surface: A date and a solver at last cracking the puzzle in front of them.
explanation.walkthrough: '1' looks like a reference to 1 Across but is the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: The puzzle appeared in the newspaper of that name, so it names the publication printing it.

clue.text: Mountaineer out for the count

indicators.note: out means the letters of mountaineer are put out of their order

explanation.surface: A climber eliminated, like a boxer down for the count.
explanation.definitionFit: An enumeration is a counting or listing, so it means a count.

clue.text: Shabby stuff besides, beating performance?

parts.note: tat is British slang for cheap or shoddy goods
too means besides, as well

explanation.surface: Cheap junk, and a drumming display as well.
explanation.definitionFit: A military tattoo is a display with drums, and a tattoo is also a drumbeat.

clue.text: Half the field in one sport, legal in another?

definitions.text: Half the field in one sport
definitions.meaning: in cricket the off side and the leg side each make up half the field
in football a player in a permitted position is not offside

explanation.surface: A comparison of rules across two sports.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side, or leg side, is half the field.
explanation.definitionFit: On side is the cricket term for the leg side, and onside in football means not offside.

clue.text: Sweet — or not?

definitions.meaning: a sweet here is a dessert, such as a pastry with fruit filling
the opposite of sweet in taste: sharp or sour

explanation.surface: A short question about whether something is sweet or not.
explanation.definitionFit: A tart is a pastry dessert, and tart as an adjective means sharp-tasting, the reverse of sweet.

clue.text: Two locos — make sure the little one's going in the right place

definitions.text: make sure the little one's going in the right place

parts.note: loco as slang means crazy, which is potty in British slang
a loco is also short for a locomotive, which pulls a train

explanation.surface: Railway talk of two engines, then a parent making sure a toddler goes in the right place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locos' is read in two senses: crazy and railway engines.
explanation.definitionFit: Toilet training a toddler teaches them to use a child's pot rather than a nappy.

clue.text: Illegal practice that's much studied in the City

parts.note: the definite article, given by the word the
the FT, the Financial Times, is read closely in the City, London's financial district

explanation.surface: A shady financial practice scrutinised by City traders.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, where the pink Financial Times is the paper of record.
explanation.definitionFit: Theft is stealing, a crime and so an unlawful practice.

clue.text: A force flying up in the distance

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the air force letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, is a flying force

explanation.surface: An air force taking off far away.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar means far away, so at a distance.

clue.text: Short suit in the bag

parts.note: brief means short
a case is a legal suit, a lawsuit

explanation.surface: A short suit packed away in a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' looks like clothing but is a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A briefcase is a flat bag for carrying papers and documents.

clue.text: Little time in the King and I for musical instruction

indicators.note: in puts the time abbreviation inside the king's name and the letter after it

parts.note: Tut is short for Tutankhamun, the boy king of Egypt
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A moment in the musical The King and I, used as a score direction.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the musical The King and I, but 'the King' is Tutankhamun.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti is a direction in a score telling all performers to play together.

clue.text: Course ahead initially among the branches?

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the word ahead

parts.note: among means in
a tree is made up of branches

explanation.surface: A racecourse where something is up ahead among the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: AINTREE is the Liverpool racecourse that hosts the Grand National steeplechase.
explanation.definitionFit: Aintree is a famous British horse-racing course, so it is an example of a course.

clue.text: Little support for pond life

parts.note: a tad means a little
a pole is a support, as for a tent

explanation.surface: Not much help on offer for the creatures living in a pond.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is a frog's larva, one of the creatures found in ponds.
